conflicts.issue: The WHO 2020 classes carcinosarcoma (and malignant mixed Müllerian tumour) as an epithelial tumour of the cervix, vagina and corpus, and lists adenosarcoma and myoepithelial carcinoma at these sites; ICCC-2017 places 8930-8935, 8950, 8980-8982 in XIIa4 at every site. The tree refers them to Group XII. Endometrial stromal sarcoma (8930) is in the same range, so it is referred to Group XII and not to Group IX.

Mesonephric adenocarcinoma is an HPV-independent adenocarcinoma of the cervix in the WHO 2020, but ICCC-2017 places 9110 in XIIa6 at every site. The tree refers it to Group XII. Mesonephric-like adenocarcinoma of the corpus (9113, not in ICD-O-3.2) waits on the registrar; if the registrar maps it to 9110/3, it goes to Group XII too.

The cervix table lists germ cell tumours; ICCC-2017 places 9071 in Xb4, 9064 in Xb1 and 9100 in Xb5 at these sites. The tree refers malignant germ cell tumours to Group X and excludes mature teratoma and dermoid cyst. An ovarian primary (C56.9) is Group X by site.

The alias index already maps 'Clear cell adenocarcinoma, NOS', 'Clear cell carcinoma, NOS', 'Endometrioid adenocarcinoma, NOS', 'Endometrioid carcinoma, NOS' and 'Adenocarcinoma, endocervical type' to Group 10 (ovary). A clerk who types them for a vaginal, cervical or uterine tumour enters Group 10 unless the search box's site check drops Group 10. Group 11 must carry these strings with site routing, and the 'Also called' row of 8310/3 and 8380/3 will list Group 10's ovarian aliases (Group 10 D21).

Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma (sarcoma botryoides) of the vagina and cervix and other sarcomas are Group IX (IXa, IXd). The alias index maps 'Sarcoma botryoides' and 'Botryoid rhabdomyosarcoma' to Group 9 already; the tree refers them.

Within Group XI: ICCC-2017 places vulva NOS (C51.9) among the skin sites (XIe), where its skin list holds no range for 8085, 8086, 8482, 8380, 8500, 8144, 8562, 8441, 8249 or 8045; and the XIf10 list holds no range for 8090, 8400, 8409 or 8413 at C51.0 to C51.8. Rule 3 keeps these codes in Group XI, but the subgroup at output is undetermined, and the skin part (XIe_skin_carcinoma) also routes C51.9. Registrar question 5.

data_gaps.need: A typed paediatric source for carcinomas of the cervix, vagina, vulva and uterus in patients aged 0 to 18: squamous cell carcinoma at the cervix and vagina, the HPV status of vulval squamous cell carcinoma, gastric-type adenocarcinoma, and the types of uterine adenocarcinoma.
data_gaps.why: Wohlmuth 2021 (SEER-18) now gives clear cell carcinoma at the cervix, adenocarcinoma at the cervix and uterus, and squamous cell carcinoma at the vulva, but it groups histology into classes (squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, melanoma, sarcoma, germ cell tumour, other) and names no further type. Pfister 2022 Table 3 lists only benign lower female genital tumours. Squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix and vagina, gastric-type adenocarcinoma and every typed endometrial carcinoma remain picker entries.
data_gaps.candidate_source: A paediatric series or registry report that gives ICD-O-3 histology codes by site at ages 0 to 19 (for example a SEER analysis by histology code); for the vagina, Herbst AL, Scully RE. Adenocarcinoma of the vagina in adolescence. A report of 7 cases including 6 clear-cell carcinomas (so-called mesonephromas). Cancer 1970;25(4):745-757 (ICCR Vagina reference 5).

data_gaps.need: A source for the report vocabulary of embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma (sarcoma botryoides) and yolk sac tumour of the vagina and cervix in children.
data_gaps.why: Wohlmuth 2021 now reports embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma as most of the vaginal and cervical sarcomas and yolk sac tumour as the second most common vaginal histology at ages 0 to 18, so both referrals have a site-specific paediatric source. Wohlmuth gives no report vocabulary and no recognition aid: the label's 'sarcoma botryoides' rests on ICD-O-3.2, which holds Sarcoma botryoides and Botryoid sarcoma as terms of 8910/3.
data_gaps.candidate_source: WHO Classification of Tumours, Paediatric Tumours, 5th edition (2022), female genital tract chapter; or a vaginal yolk sac tumour or botryoid rhabdomyosarcoma case series.
